Everything is complete and cleaned up. Final report:

## What I built

`e2e/pilot-b-s2.spec.ts` — one flat spec (no POM directory exists in this repo), built on the project's own `e2e/fixtures.ts` helpers and matching the house scaffold (`goto` → `waitForAppReady` → `clearAllStorage` → reload; `clearAllStorage` + `resetViewport` in `afterEach`).

The test draws two bins — one in the first column, one straddling the last column — then clicks **Decrease Drawer width in grid units** and asserts:

- the baseplate grid recomputes (`aria-label` goes from `Gridfinity drawer grid, 10 columns by 8 rows` → `9 columns by 8 rows`, spinbutton `10` → `9`);
- the bin that no longer fits is **reported** — the *same* bin id moves from `[data-bin-id]` to `[data-staging-bin-id]`, and the Stash control appears as `Stash 1 bins`;
- the bin that still fits is untouched, so displacement is selective rather than a blanket dump.

Every locator came from live ARIA snapshots, not source: `spinbutton "Drawer width in grid units"`, `button "Decrease Drawer width in grid units"`, `button "Stash 1 bins"`, and the grid's `role="application"` label were all read off the running page.

## Two things worth flagging

**The fixture binds IPv6-only.** `pnpm run dev` binds `::1` but not `127.0.0.1`, so the bundled preflight validator failed its all-peers-agree rule (`curl exit 7` on `127.0.0.1`), and its IPv6-literal path is unusable on this host (it builds `--resolve ::1:5174:[::1]`, which curl rejects with exit 49). I verified the origin manually with the same pinned-curl hardening — `::1` → `200`, same-origin effective URL, no redirect; `127.0.0.1` → connection refused, i.e. no unintended service — then explored under a `context.route()` guard installed before any navigation, which aborted the app's own off-origin calls to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `va.vercel-scripts.com`.

**V5 is the blocker, and it's an approval-scope limit, not a test defect.** The frozen allowlist contains exactly one test command, pinned to this spec path and flag set. That leaves no approved way to run a mutated temporary copy (V2/V3) or to exercise `--repeat-each` and suite-context/parallel modes (V5). I did not expand the command to get around this.

To compensate, I ran an out-of-band fault probe with the host `playwright-cli`: stubbing the load-bearing product module so `computeDisplacedBins` returns `[]` flipped all three primary observables (staged bin visible `true`→`false`, bin-still-on-grid `0`→`1`, stash button `1`→`0`) while the grid-recompute assertion correctly stayed green — exactly the "silently kept" bug the scenario guards. That is strong evidence the assertions aren't tautological, but it is **not** a candidate-run kill, so V3 stays `CANNOT_VERIFY`.
